title: Reducedness descends from a split completed geometric stalk
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal with $F=S/\mathfrak p$ finite separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $K/k$ be any extension field and $\iota:F\hookrightarrow K$ a $k$-embedding. Define
$$\mathfrak q=\ker(S\otimes_kK\longrightarrow K),\quad s\otimes\lambda\longmapsto\iota(\bar s)\lambda,\qquad B=(S\otimes_kK)_{\mathfrak q},\quad\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qB,$$
where tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and let $\widehat B$ be the $\mathfrak n$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. (1) For every field $L$, the ring $L[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] has no nonzero nilpotent elements; more precisely $h\mapsto(h(u,0),h(0,v))$ induces an injective ring map $L[[u,v]]/(uv)\to L[[u]]\times L[[v]]$. (2) The canonical maps $A\to B\to\widehat B$ are injective. (3) If $\widehat B$ is isomorphic as a ring, without requiring $K$-linearity, to $K[[u,v]]/(uv)$, then $\widehat B$, $B$ and $A$ have no nonzero nilpotent elements. Quotient rings and algebra maps use [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. No algebraic closedness assumption on $K$ and no dimension assumption on $S$ is made.

proof.text: Write $h=\sum_{i,j\geq0}a_{ij}u^iv^j$. Define $E(h)=(\sum_i a_{i0}u^i,\sum_j a_{0j}v^j)$. The coefficientwise addition and convolution product of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] show that $E$ preserves $1$, addition and multiplication: in the coefficient of $u^n v^0$ of a product, both contributing $v$-exponents must be zero, and similarly on the other axis. Moreover $E(h)=0$ exactly when $a_{i0}=a_{0j}=0$ for every $i,j$. In that case define $g=\sum_{i,j\geq0}a_{i+1,j+1}u^iv^j$; coefficientwise $h=uvg$. Conversely $E(uvg)=0$. Thus $\ker E=(uv)$. By the quotient construction [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $E$ induces a ring map $\overline E:L[[u,v]]/(uv)\to L[[u]]\times L[[v]]$. If $\overline E([h])=0$, then $h\in(uv)$ by the calculation, so $[h]=0$; applying this to a difference proves injectivity.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (3)=>(1), split quadratic case; explicit coefficient calculation supplying the reducedness argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain] with the domain $L$ and one variable to obtain that $L[[u]]$ and $L[[v]]$ are domains. If $z^r=0$ in $L[[u,v]]/(uv)$, with $r\geq1$, both components of $\overline E(z)$ have $r$th power zero. A domain has no nonzero element with a zero positive power (induct on $r$ using the absence of zero divisors), so both components vanish. Step 1 then gives $z=0$. This proves all of (1).

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (3)=>(1), reducedness of the split completed quadric

proof.text: The data $k,S,\mathfrak p,F,K,\iota$ satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-trf-separable-evaluation-local-base-change]: $S$ is finite type, $F/k$ is finite separable, and $\iota$ is a $k$-embedding into the extension field $K$. Its $C,\epsilon,\mathfrak q,A,B$ are exactly the rings and maps in the statement. It gives that $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings and the canonical $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. Apply the injectivity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] to this map to obtain $A\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), (1) and its affine proof; algebra.tex Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective)

proof.text: Step 3 gives that $B$ is Noetherian local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qB$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] to $(B,\mathfrak n)$: its completion is exactly the specified $\widehat B=\varprojlim_r B/\mathfrak n^r$, and the canonical $B\to\widehat B$ is faithfully flat. The injectivity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] therefore gives $B\hookrightarrow\widehat B$. Together with step 3 this proves (2).

Assume a ring isomorphism $\phi:\widehat B\xrightarrow{\sim}K[[u,v]]/(uv)$. If $x^r=0$ in $\widehat B$, with $r\geq1$, then $\phi(x)^r=0$, so step 2 with $L=K$ gives $\phi(x)=0$, and injectivity of $\phi$ gives $x=0$. If $b^r=0$ in $B$, its image in $\widehat B$ is zero by the preceding conclusion, so $b=0$ by step 4. If $a^r=0$ in $A$, its image in $B$ is zero, so $a=0$ by step 3. This proves (3). This argument uses only preservation of multiplication and zero by the ring maps, so $\phi$ need not respect $K$-scalars.

lean.statement: theorem split_completion_local_invariant_descent (k : Type u) (S : Type v) (K : Type w) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Field K] [Algebra k S] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (p : Ideal S) [p.IsMaximal] [FiniteDimensional k (S ⧸ p)] [Algebra.IsSeparable k (S ⧸ p)] (ι : (S ⧸ p) →ₐ[k] K) : ∃ f : Localization.AtPrime p →+* geometricStalk p ι, (∀ s : S, f (algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime p) s) = algebraMap (S ⊗[k] K) (geometricStalk p ι) (s ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : K))) ∧ Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Injective (algebraMap (geometricStalk p ι) (completedGeometricStalk p ι)) ∧ (Nonempty (completedGeometricStalk p ι ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) K ⧸ Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) K) * MvPowerSeries.X 1})) → IsReduced (completedGeometricStalk p ι) ∧ IsReduced (geometricStalk p ι) ∧ IsReduced (Localization.AtPrime p))
